added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: great moderation, um where we had a long stretch of low inflation and steady economic growth
added_claims.claim: The Greenspan era (late 1980s to 2006) is remembered as the Great Moderation, a long stretch of low inflation and steady growth that ran almost to the financial crisis, and the crisis is linked by many to the Fed's policy in the run-up.
added_claims.testable: partly - volatility regimes can be measured, causal link to Fed policy is narrative

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: Now Walsh, interestingly enough, is kind of moving towards the the Greenspan or maybe the pre-Greenspan era in terms of not really wanting to to share too much
added_claims.claim: Fed communication went from a statement of a couple of hundred words in 1994 to meeting notes, projections and press conferences; the new chair is moving back toward minimal communication and no forecasts, a reversal of the transparency regime.
added_claims.indicator: Fed communication volume (statement, SEP, press conference)
added_claims.testable: partly - communication regime change dates are observable, market effect is not tested here

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: the academics validate what the central bank is doing. And so they'll they'll sort of say that yes, what they do make sense from our perspective. That doesn't mean it's good policy.
added_claims.claim: A fourth layer of Fed politics is the academics, whose models validate whatever the central bank does; this validation shows internal consistency, not that the policy is good, so academic support is weak evidence of sound policy.

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: it has also become very much in vogue to talk about economic trend where you look actually at economic data and it's been doing very well for those who have done that the last couple of years
added_claims.claim: Trend models built on economic data (rather than prices) have done very well in the last couple of years and have become fashionable, so their exposure to data-quality changes matters.
added_claims.conditions: performance is recent; data-quality changes may break it
added_claims.testable: partly - needs a defined economic-trend strategy and track record

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: A trend follower will say that that I just need to look at the prices themselves. The other information may be more backward-looking or it doesn't update it as quickly.
added_claims.claim: The pure price-trend argument against fundamentals is that macro information is backward-looking and updates slowly, so prices already carry the useful information; Mark sees a middle ground where fundamentals corroborate price trends.
added_claims.testable: yes - compare price-only and price-plus-fundamental trend systems

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: forward guidance may have served a purpose when we are at the the zero bound. But, now we'll sort of say that it's the actions that should drive prices and drive markets.
added_claims.claim: Forward guidance was useful at the zero lower bound but now actions should drive prices, so diminishing its importance removes speech-driven noise from market prices.
added_claims.conditions: effective at the zero bound; less needed once rates are above zero
added_claims.testable: partly - event-study of price noise around Fed communication

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: it, i.e. the banks, somehow with some kind of rule uh that, you know, makes it more um tenable for banks to own more bonds and whatever.
added_claims.claim: If the Fed steps back from buying Treasuries it may push banks to become the buyer through regulatory rules, so the identity of the owner may matter less than the fact that heavy debt supply still has to be absorbed.
added_claims.indicator: Treasury issuance; bank Treasury holdings; bank capital rules
added_claims.testable: partly - bank holdings and issuance are observable, rule changes are not specified

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: we would like to have the people who buy or sell bonds are doing it because they have clear profit objectives.
added_claims.claim: Bond prices are more informative when the marginal buyers and sellers are profit-motivated rather than driven by policy or regulation, which is the market structure that favours trend followers and price discovery.

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: that's good because then you're going to reduce the noise and you're going to and you're going to increase the link between the economics and and prices
added_claims.claim: In the long run better official data reduces noise and tightens the link between economic fundamentals and prices, which would help data-driven systems, even though poor data hurts them in the short run.
added_claims.conditions: long run only; short run the data quality is poor
added_claims.testable: partly - measure data-signal predictive power before and after revisions

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: I'm always kind of concerned that there probably is a motivation in terms of changing the way data is collected and what data is even collected.
added_claims.claim: Changes to what official data is collected and how may be motivated by making the data look better, which is a data-integrity risk for fundamental and economic-trend systems and a reason to trust prices more.

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: productivity is is is going to be important for the global growth because right now global growth is is relatively poor.
added_claims.claim: Global growth is currently relatively weak, so a productivity boom from AI would matter for fundamental prices more than for trend followers directly.
added_claims.testable: partly - productivity and growth series exist

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: you can think of competition within your industry, but if let's say that there are players outside your industry that might have an impact on your business
added_claims.claim: An allocator chooses among more than ten hedge fund strategies, so managed futures should be evaluated against the whole strategy universe, not only against other CTAs.
added_claims.testable: yes - cross-strategy comparison on common data

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: obviously you can be the right on the right side with your uh with your tail risk strategy, but in my favorite would of course be something like trend following
added_claims.claim: In high-risk regimes tail-risk strategies are on the right side, but the host prefers trend following as the diversifier for a high-VIX environment.
added_claims.direction: long trend following or tail risk in high-VIX regimes

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: Now, the same also applies to global macro, but the coefficient is negative.
added_claims.claim: Global macro, like managed futures, shows an insignificant sensitivity to the high-risk regime but with a negative coefficient, so it should be given less weight as a high-VIX diversifier.
added_claims.indicator: global macro hedge fund excess return vs VIX regime
added_claims.testable: yes - regression on hedge fund indices

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: in the case of managed futures trend following it's been pretty solid 12 months
added_claims.claim: The past 12 months were unusually uncertain, and managed futures trend following had a solid year, consistent with the regime finding.
added_claims.indicator: managed futures performance over the last 12 months

added_claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
added_claims.quote: there's more likely that there's going to be some disconnect uh that there's going to be some uh change in the environment so that so that your strategy may not be as effective
added_claims.claim: Long-short and structured strategies fail in high-volatility regimes because relationships they rely on disconnect and the environment changes, which explains the negative alpha found in those regimes.
added_claims.indicator: long-short and structured trade performance in high vol
added_claims.testable: partly - the study shows the effect, not the mechanism

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: We did some analysis on our side at Dawn also in a similar vein in terms of analyzing different alternative investment strategies versus trend following and and and obviously we come to to similar conclusions.
added_claims.claim: The host's own firm analysis of alternative strategies versus trend following reached similar conclusions to Mark's VIX-regime study, which is independent supporting evidence.

completeness_estimate: 0.80 - first reader covered the Fed-chair, trend-concentration and VIX-regime study ideas well; missed side arguments (Fed communication history, bank bond buying, profit-motive pricing, data-integrity concerns, global macro result, host's corroboration) and the Great Moderation framing.
